📲 SLIDE 1 – WHAT IS AUTISM?

👩‍👦 Parent: What is autism, doctor?

👨‍⚕️ Doctor:
Autism is a developmental condition that affects communication, behavior, and social interaction.
It means your child experiences the world in a unique way 💙

📲 SLIDE 2 – EARLY SIGNS

👩‍👦 Parent: My child doesn’t respond, avoids eye contact… is it normal?

👨‍⚕️ Doctor:
These can be early signs of autism:
Early identification is important.

📲 SLIDE 3 – PARENT CONCERN

👩‍👦 Parent: Did I do something wrong?

👨‍⚕️ Doctor:
No, it’s NOT your fault 💙
Autism is related to brain development — not parenting.

📲 SLIDE 4 – SOLUTION + CTA

👩‍👦 Parent: What should I do now?

• No eye contact 👀
• Not responding to name
• Delayed speech 🗣️
• Prefers to play alone
• Repetitive behaviors
• Difficulty in communication
• Limited social interaction
• Strong routines or habits

🏷️ TITLE:

WORLD HEALTH DAY 2026 🌍💙
KNOW EARLY SIGNS BY AGE

📲 SLIDE 1 – INTRO

Healthy children grow with timely care 💙

Knowing early signs by age can help you take the right step at the right time.

📲 SLIDE 2 – 0 to 1 YEAR

EARLY SIGNS (0–1 YEAR)

• No smiling 😊
• Limited eye contact 👀
• Doesn’t respond to sounds
• Poor head control

📲 SLIDE 3 – 1 to 2 YEARS

EARLY SIGNS (1–2 YEARS)

• No single words
• Not responding to name
• No pointing or gestures
• Limited interaction

📲 SLIDE 4 – 2 to 3 YEARS

EARLY SIGNS (2–3 YEARS)

• Delayed speech 🗣️
• Repetitive behaviors
• Difficulty in understanding
• Prefers to play alone

📲 SLIDE 5 – 3+ YEARS

EARLY SIGNS (3+ YEARS)

• Poor social interaction
• Difficulty in communication
• Trouble following instructions
• Strong routines or habits

📲 SLIDE 6 – CTA

DON’T IGNORE EARLY SIGNS

Early identification leads to better development 🌟

🏷️ TREATMENT FOR AUTISM 💙

Autism has no single cure, but the right support can help children grow and thrive 🌟

Effective Therapies Include:
• Behavioral Therapy
• Speech Therapy 🗣️
• Occupational Therapy
• Social Skills Training

Parental Support Matters:
• Follow structured routines
• Practice therapy activities at home
• Stay consistent and patient
